solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In company of bread retailer, single mum's caught early transport

indicators.note: the baker's name catches and holds the other pieces between its letters

parts.note: a baker sells bread
single means one
mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A single mother rides along with the baker on some old-fashioned vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A boneshaker was a Victorian bicycle with solid tyres. 'In company of' only joins, and 'mum' means silent, not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A boneshaker was the nickname for an early bicycle with iron tyres and no springs, so a historic means of travel.

clue.text: Actor old, comparatively energetic, omitting line

indicators.note: omitting tells us to drop some letters from the comparative adjective

parts.note: more energetic is livelier
EL is an elevated railway line, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: An ageing actor is described as more lively, except in delivering his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitting' removes EL from the middle of LIVELIER, leaving LIVIER; the obvious L for line leaves the wrong letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and film performer.

clue.text: Recording studios finally getting decoration here in Surrey

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of studios

parts.note: the OM, Order of Merit, is an honour or decoration

explanation.surface: Sound studios eventually get redecorated in a Surrey location.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a Surrey town, home of the Derby horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points to a place in the county of Surrey, and Epsom is a town there.

clue.text: Archbishop distributed cigars in presence of cardinal?

indicators.note: letters handed out and spread around are rearranged

parts.note: HE, His Eminence, is the formal style of a cardinal

explanation.surface: Cigars are handed round in the presence of a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges CIGARS together with HE; 'in presence of' joins them. The question mark flags that a cardinal gives only an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: His Grace is the formal style used when addressing or referring to an archbishop.

clue.text: Relax and don't gamble excessively!

definitions.meaning: an idiomatic instruction to calm down and not get agitated
literally, don't bet so much that you lose even the shirt you are wearing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stay calm, and read literally warns against betting the clothes off your back.

clue.text: Accept as inevitable singer's development

indicators.note: a development changes the form of something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A vocalist's career progresses and must be accepted as it comes.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's adds no letter; 'development' rearranges SINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign oneself to something is to accept it as unavoidable.

clue.text: English writer created racy annual book, nothing left out

indicators.note: created means made up, so the letters are formed into something new
left out means one letter is removed from the word book

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A British author has written a racy yearbook with nothing omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes one O from BOOK, leaving BOK, and 'created' rearranges RACY ANNUAL BOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Ayckbourn is a prolific English playwright, known for comedies of suburban life.

clue.text: See 7
Fair length of time needed to arrest woman

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: an age is a long period
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Police take a while to detain a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as just or pale but means middling; 'needed' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of middling or ordinary matches average, as in a fair performance.

clue.text: Boo coming from this spectator

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A jeer comes from a member of the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To boo and to hiss are both ways an audience shows disapproval.

clue.text: One predicts the future — straw fabric

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
a drinking straw is something you suck through, a sucker

explanation.surface: A fortune teller sells straw cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a thin puckered cotton or linen cloth, usually striped.

clue.text: Season with another ingredient and gently boil

indicators.note: one letter of the word is swapped for a different one put in

parts.note: summer is a season of the year

explanation.surface: A cook seasons a dish, adds another ingredient and lets it bubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with another ingredient' swaps the U of SUMMER for I; the cookery surface hides that Season is a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: To simmer is to cook just below boiling point, bubbling gently.

clue.text: Spiritualist to tolerate animated character

parts.note: a yogi is a spiritual master of yoga
to bear is to put up with

explanation.surface: A mystic learns to put up with a cartoon figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogi Bear is a Hanna-Barbera cartoon bear.

clue.text: Type of wine workmen said accompany good bread in Durban

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and the rand is South Africa's currency, used in Durban

indicators.note: said means we want a word that sounds like the one given

parts.note: a crew is a team of workers

explanation.surface: Labourers are told to have good bread with their wine in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns CREW into the French CRU, which sounds the same; 'accompany' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand cru is a top-ranked wine or vineyard classification in France.

clue.text: Sharp-eyed types reported man on board slow to work

indicators.note: reported means we take a word that sounds like the chess piece

parts.note: a knight is a piece, or man, on a chessboard

indicators.note: put to work, the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Observant people are said to be slow to get on with the job aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' gives NIGHT from KNIGHT, and 'to work' rearranges SLOW. 'on board' suggests a ship but means a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Night owls stay up late; owls see well in the dark, hence the playful sharp-eyed.

clue.text: Waste matter mired in bureaucracy

indicators.note: mired in says the answer is stuck inside the next word

explanation.surface: Wasteful material is bogged down in official red tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the nitrogen compound in which the body excretes waste, in urine.

clue.text: Stumble upon, outside of tiny church, a work of art

parts.note: to trip is to stumble

indicators.note: outside of takes the outer letters of the word tiny

explanation.surface: Someone trips over a small church's artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside of' gives TY from TINY; 'upon' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych is a painting or carving on three hinged panels, often an altarpiece.

clue.text: George repeatedly wins cooking award

indicators.note: wins is read as takes in, so the doubled letter holds the other piece
repeatedly says the letter is written out twice

parts.note: on means cooking, as in the dinner is on

explanation.surface: A man named George keeps winning a culinary prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wins' is read as takes in, so GG holds ON. Gong is British slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is slang for a medal or honour, any award.

clue.text: Lady speaker having beef about rogue state

indicators.note: about means around, so the animal goes around the other pieces

parts.note: beef comes from the ox
a rat is a scoundrel
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A female orator has a grievance about a rogue nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like a complaint but is the animal; 'having' only joins. Rhode Island is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratrix is the feminine form of orator, a woman who makes speeches.

clue.text: Country is sprinkled with manure

indicators.note: sprinkled means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A land is spread with fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprinkled with' rearranges IS and MANURE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Suriname is a country on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Folly reflected embankment on headland

indicators.note: a reflection runs back to front, so the barrier word is read backwards

parts.note: a dam is a barrier bank
a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness place names

explanation.surface: A foolish embankment is mirrored on a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns DAM into MAD; 'on' joins in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Folly and madness both mean foolishness or senseless behaviour.

clue.text: Exotic tree, with a snake sliding up, attracted by bees

indicators.note: drawn in by the insects, so they surround the other letters

parts.note: B is a bee, and two make BB

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up reads the letters backwards

parts.note: a boa is a constrictor snake

explanation.surface: An unusual tree, with a snake climbing it, draws in the bees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliding up' turns A BOA into AOBA, which 'attracted by' places between B and B.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is an African tree with a huge swollen trunk.

clue.text: Retraced international markets, before meal, for meat

indicators.note: retraced means gone back over, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: marts are markets
AP stands for ante prandium, Latin for before a meal, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone retraces steps through world markets before dinner to buy meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retraced' turns the whole run IMARTSAP backwards; AP is the prescription abbreviation for before meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked beef, a deli staple.

clue.text: It's a travesty wages inhibit staff

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold in, so the pay contains the rod

parts.note: pay is wages
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Employees complain that low pay holding back staff is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but means a stick; 'It's a' only joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation, which is what a parody is.

clue.text: Motorcyclist delivered leads to electronic retailer

parts.note: delivered means freed or rid

indicators.note: leads to means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A biker dropped off cables for an electronics shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' suggests cables but means first letters; the pick gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is someone who rides a motorbike or horse.

clue.text: Hob that is scrubbed by Elizabeth making pudding

indicators.note: scrubbed means cancelled or wiped out, so letters are removed

parts.note: a hob is a hobgoblin, a household sprite like a brownie
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
Betty is a pet form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Elizabeth cleans the cooker while making a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrubbed' removes IE from BROWNIE; 'Hob' looks like the cooker top but is a sprite. Brown Betty is a baked apple and breadcrumb pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown Betty is a baked dessert of apples layered with sweetened breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Active person initially rescues man out of extension window

indicators.note: out of means the letters are taken away from the window

parts.note: a dormer is a window set in a roof extension

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of rescues

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for man, or male

explanation.surface: An energetic person saves a man who has fallen out of a loft window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R and M from DORMER, leaving DOER.
explanation.definitionFit: A doer is someone who gets things done, a person of action.

clue.text: Coordinates equipment for lumberjack

definitions.meaning: plural of axis, the reference lines of a graph
the tools a woodcutter uses for chopping, plural of axe

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the plural of axis, graph lines, and of axe, the chopping tool.

clue.text: Court officials crowd lift

parts.note: the bench is the judges or magistrates of a court
to press is to crowd

explanation.surface: Judges crowd into an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: A bench press is a weightlifting exercise, a lift done lying on a bench.
